title: Introduction to cancer evolution, cell of origin and the microenvironment
why: The lecturer introduces the fifth lecture of the series and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer evolution, the microenvironment, and Darwinian selection.

title: Evidence for mutation-driven clonal evolution and selection
why: The lecturer explains how cancers evolve through successive clonal mutations and selective advantages using pre-neoplastic sequencing data, mouse esophageal models, and human eyelid tissue studies.

title: Epigenetic disruption as a driver of tumor development
why: The lecturer explores how transient chromatin and transcriptional remodeling, evidenced by Polycomb repressive complex studies in Drosophila, can drive tumorigenesis independently of DNA mutations.

title: Stem cell properties and stochastic versus hierarchical models of cancer
why: The lecturer examines the hierarchy of normal tissue differentiation and compares stem cell properties to cancer development using leukemia and intestinal crypt APC knockout models.

title: Evidence for cancer stem cells and tumor hierarchy in leukemia
why: The lecturer moves from theoretical models of cancer hierarchy to examining experimental evidence for cancer stem cells in leukemia and clarifying related terminology.

title: Cell of origin and APC loss in intestinal tumor initiation
why: The lecturer turns to solid tumors, examining the intestinal crypt model and APC knockout experiments to identify the cell of origin in colorectal cancer.

title: Pollution-induced inflammation and stemness in lung cancer promotion
why: The lecturer demonstrates that genetic mutations require permissive environmental and inflammatory stimuli to progress to malignancy, highlighting pollution in lung cancer and colitis in colon cancer.

title: Inflammation-induced stemness and tumor formation in APC-deficient intestinal progenitors
why: The lecturer examines how chronic inflammation or K-RAS mutation cooperates with APC loss to activate NF-kappa B and induce a stem cell signature in the colon.

title: Stromal support of established tumors and microenvironment-targeted therapy
why: The lecturer discusses stromal dependence in established tumors, potential microenvironment-targeted therapies, and modern single-cell and spatial profiling methodologies used to map tumor interactions.

title: Investigating cancer evolution and cell interactions with single-cell and spatial omics
why: it explains the experimental and computational techniques used to investigate human tumor biology and cellular interactions in the lab

title: Lecture summary: mutations, cell identity and microenvironment in cancer evolution
why: The lecturer synthesizes how genetics, cell type properties, transcriptional plasticity, and environmental promoters converge through an evolutionary process to produce cancer.

title: Lecture close: next lecture on cancer therapy
why: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the topic for the following lecture.
